claim: IEEE conference acceptance rates typically range from 20% to 50%, varying with conference prestige and topic relevance.
stance_target: students should expect substantial rejection risk even at ordinary IEEE conferences
quoted_support: IEEE conferences maintain rigorous standards. Acceptance rates can vary widely, typically ranging from 20% to 50%.

claim: Lack of novelty/significant contribution is the single most common reason IEEE conference papers are rejected.
stance_target: novelty is the top selection criterion reviewers apply to IEEE conference submissions
quoted_support: Lack of Novelty or Significant Contribution: The most common reason. Your paper must present a clear, new idea or a significant improvement over existing work.

claim: Major formatting and guideline violations (wrong template, page limits, missing required sections) can cause desk rejection without technical review at IEEE conferences.
stance_target: formatting compliance as a precondition for review at IEEE venues
quoted_support: Major Formatting and Guideline Violations: Ignoring page limits, using the wrong template, or missing required sections (like abstracts or keywords) can lead to a desk rejection without technical review.

claim: Insufficient comparison with state-of-the-art methods and lack of statistical significance are cited as common evaluation weaknesses leading to rejection.
stance_target: rigorous evaluation/benchmarking is required for IEEE paper acceptance
quoted_support: Poor Experimental Design or Evaluation: Flawed methodology, inadequate data, insufficient comparisons with state-of-the-art methods, or lack of statistical significance can lead to immediate rejection.
